title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Momentum Opportunity

epigraph.quote: Never argue with the tape. Fundamentals tell you what to buy; the trend tells you when the market agrees with you.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein

web_blocks.html: Pass 1 established that Coforge clears our fundamental compounder bar, with a watch on post-Encora debt and DSO. Next, Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis asks whether institutions are accumulating the stock right now. As of November 16, 2026, Coforge is in a confirmed Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend (Week 16) [24]. The stock has gained +17.88% since its Stage 2 breakout and +45.28% over six months [24].

web_blocks.takeaway: Technical timing gate is CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION (BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO): Coforge sits in a tight 10.76% Bollinger-band VCP squeeze just +4.35% above its 10-week EMA, offering a disciplined entry without chasing.

web_blocks.html: Broader market context also supports selective Stage 2 leadership. On November 16, 2026, India's market regime stood in an Uptrend (narrow breadth), with 73.9% of tracked stocks above their 50-DMA and 3 distribution days. FIIs/FPIs bought a net +₹4,864.68 Cr in the cash market, offsetting DII selling of -₹3,519.05 Cr (+₹1,345.63 Cr combined) [23]. Narrow breadth funnels capital into visible earnings compounders like Coforge [5].

The chart shows a textbook Stage 2 Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP). After rallying +45.28% from its ₹1,008.10 low, price has coiled between ₹1,956 and ₹2,128 [24]. Bollinger bandwidth is tight at 10.76%, and volume has dried up to 0.83x the 30-day average [24]. A high-volume breakout above ₹2,150 (Pivot R1) targets ₹2,255 (Pivot R2) and ₹2,400+. Conversely, a break below ₹1,913 (50-DMA) and ₹1,851.80 (S1) signals deeper digestion. Our hard structural stop sits at ₹1,659.40, just below the 30-week SMA (₹1,692.22) and Pivot S2 (₹1,658.60). On the November 16 ledger, 20-day volume ratio was quiet at 0.59x and 28-day relative strength was -3.60%, reinforcing our staged dip-accumulation approach.

book_paragraphs: Once you know a business is worth owning, the most expensive mistake in investing is buying it at the wrong point in its market cycle—chasing a vertical spike 30% above its 10-week moving average, only to get shaken out during a routine 15% pullback. That is why you and I always read the tape before committing capital.

On November 16, 2026, Coforge's chart tells a remarkably constructive story. Using Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis, the stock is in Week 16 of a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend. Since breaking out into Stage 2, it has gained 17.88%, and over the past six months it is up 45.28% from its base. Yet unlike parabolic momentum stocks that leave investors stranded far above support, Coforge has paused just 4.08% below its 52-week high of ₹2,127.90 to digest those gains.

Look closely at the moving-average architecture. At ₹2,010.00, the stock sits just 1.60% above its 20-day EMA (₹2,008.95), 4.35% above its 10-week EMA (₹1,956.01), and 6.68% above its 50-day SMA (₹1,913.25). Meanwhile, the primary 30-week SMA sits way down at ₹1,692.22 and is sloping steadily upward. In institutional trend-following, anything within 5% to 8% of the 10-week EMA in a Stage 2 uptrend is considered a prime, non-extended buy zone.

Even better, the volatility profile confirms that weak hands are being absorbed quietly. Bollinger bandwidth has compressed to 10.76%—a classic Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP)—while 14-day RSI sits at a balanced 58.05 on the daily chart, 65.47 on the weekly chart, and 53.67 on the 4-hour chart. There is zero overbought exhaustion here. Volume on the November 16 session was 1.95 million shares, or 0.83x the 30-day average of 2.34 million, showing that sellers are stepping back as price coils near ₹2,040.

What about the broader Indian market backdrop? On November 16, the Nifty regime is in an Uptrend with narrow breadth (73.9% of tracked stocks above their 50-DMA and 3 distribution days). Foreign institutional investors were net buyers of +₹4,864.68 Cr in the cash market, offsetting domestic outflows of -₹3,519.05 Cr. In narrow-breadth uptrends, institutional money crowds into companies with undeniable earnings momentum—and Coforge's Q2 FY27 margin raise and $1.04B order intake fit that bill.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Respecting the 30-Week Floor
book_callouts.text: A tight VCP squeeze near ₹2,010 gives you an immediate tactical edge, but never confuse a tight entry with zero risk. Your structural invalidation stop sits at ₹1,659.40—just below the rising 30-week SMA (₹1,692.22) and Pivot S2 (₹1,658.60). If Coforge ever slices through that floor on heavy volume, the Stage 2 thesis is broken and you exit without debate.

book_subsections.title: Multi-Timeframe Levels: 1W, 1D, and 4H Alignment
paragraphs: When we inspect Coforge across three timeframes—Weekly (1W), Daily (1D), and 4-Hour (4H)—all three point in the same direction without divergence. On the 4H chart, price holds above both the 20-period EMA (₹2,029.34) and 50-period SMA (₹1,991.90) with RSI at 53.67, showing clean short-term support right around ₹2,000–₹2,030.

On the Daily chart, Pivot R1 sits at ₹2,150.00—just above the 52-week high of ₹2,127.90. A high-volume breakout above ₹2,150 opens the door to Pivot R2 at ₹2,255.00 in the short term. On the downside, initial support sits at ₹1,926.67–₹2,039.08 (spanning the 50-day SMA and 20-day EMA), followed by a major structural shelf at Pivot S1 (₹1,851.80) and final Stage 2 invalidation at ₹1,659.40.

book_subsections.title: Volume, Accumulation & Why Narrow Breadth Favors Leaders
paragraphs: One of the subtler clues on Coforge's November 16, 2026 tape is the contrast between price action and volume during its recent 1-week pause (-1.02%). Pullbacks on light volume—0.83x the 30-day average—tell us that institutional funds who accumulated during the +45.28% six-month rally are not distributing shares; rather, short-term traders are simply taking modest profits just below the ₹2,127.90 52-week high.

In a narrow-breadth market uptrend where 73.9% of tracked stocks sit above their 50-DMA and FIIs just injected +₹4,864.68 Cr in a single cash session, leadership stocks with tight VCP bases (10.76% Bollinger bandwidth) often resolve upward before laggards catch up. Watch for a decisive daily close above ₹2,150.00 (Pivot R1) on at least 1.5x average volume (>3.5M shares) as confirmation that the next Stage 2 leg toward ₹2,255–₹2,400 is underway.

book_subsections.title: Managing Drawdowns: What Would Invalidate the Stage 2 Thesis?
paragraphs: Discipline means defining your exit before you ever click buy. On the weekly chart, Coforge's Stage 2 uptrend is anchored by the rising 30-week simple moving average at ₹1,692.22 and Pivot S2 at ₹1,658.60. Routine pullbacks toward the 10-week EMA (₹1,956.01) or 50-day SMA (₹1,913.25) on light volume are healthy shakeouts that offer Tranche 2 accumulation opportunities.

However, if Coforge ever suffers a high-volume breakdown through Pivot S1 (₹1,851.80) and closes a week below ₹1,659.40, the Stage 2 structure is officially broken. At that point, the tape would be telling us that institutional funds are exiting—perhaps due to an Encora client loss or margin miss—and we respect the stop without hesitation.
